description: This team represents Juan Seguin High School's Computer Science club.
summary:
Players take on the role of a NASA missions coordinator, guiding a space program from its first satellite launch to a planned Mars colony. Developed in Godot 4.7 with pixel-art visuals, the game asks players to manage budget, research, payload mass, scientific instruments, and launch vehicles as they undertake missions around Earth, the Moon, asteroids, and Mars. Every choice involves trade-offs: larger rockets can carry heavier payloads but cost more, while insufficient capacity or research can cause a mission to fail.

The game addresses the challenge by turning space mission design into an interactive planning experience. Its mission progression shows why early infrastructure, communications, and resource scouting matter before attempting more complex exploration and settlement goals. This is important because real space exploration depends on careful budgeting, engineering decisions, and incremental progress. The game makes those interconnected challenges engaging and helps players see that reaching Mars depends on the missions that come before it.
details:
Our project is a pixel-art space mission design game built with Godot 4.7. Players take on the role of a mission coordinator and guide a campaign from an initial Earth-orbit satellite to a Mars colony. Before each launch, they choose a rocket and scientific instrument, balancing budget, payload mass, research requirements, and mission objectives. A plan that meets the requirements succeeds and advances the program; insufficient launcher capacity or research can cause a mission to fail. The campaign introduces challenges in stages, from orbital infrastructure and lunar exploration to asteroid prospecting and colony preparation.

The game makes systems-engineering concepts approachable by showing how planning decisions affect mission outcomes. It highlights why funding, mass limits, research, and earlier infrastructure matter to long-term exploration. Our team focused on turning these interconnected constraints into clear choices while keeping play engaging through pixel-art visuals, scrollable missions, and animated launches. By making mission planning interactive, the project encourages players to think about the work behind space exploration and how reaching Mars depends on successful steps along the way.
